check-ci-filters.sh takes about 140 s and runs `go list -deps` with GOPROXY=off over an empty module cache. It is the one check that catches an import which changes which CI jobs a file starts, and nothing in the Go suites can stand in for it: run it after any change to a Go import graph that cmd/dispatch, cmd/legion or cmd/listener reach.

The evidence harness is /legion/scratch/tmp/infra627 (build.sh, e1.sh, e2.sh, e2-bytes.sh, e2-dryrun.sh); the tester's is /legion/scratch/tmp/t627 (e4.sh, e5.sh, e6.sh). Both build each envoy-dispatch from a git archive export of its commit, so re-running at another head is one edit of build.sh's HEAD_COMMIT.

discoveredComplexity: A new import can be a CI defect with no test to catch it. internal/dispatch/redeliver importing internal/kvwatch widened what five gates read through `go list -deps ./cmd/dispatch` while their path filters stayed as they were, so a later change to internal/kvwatch would have skipped those jobs on the pull request and again on main, where nothing re-runs them. Only .github/scripts/check-ci-filters.sh sees it, and it is not in the fast local lane any Go change runs.
docs-pages.yaml carries a flattened copy of ci.yaml's *dispatch_server, and the check holds the two equal, so a pattern added to that anchor has to be added in both files.

Three comments in docs-pages.yaml label their flattened blocks with pattern counts that are already wrong and were wrong when they were last written: `*dispatch_server, 42 patterns` over a block of 49 (50 after this change, against the anchor's 53), `*bun_install, 16 patterns` over 15, and `*legion_command, 57 patterns` over 59. Nothing reads them: ci_filter_coverage.py has no count logic, and rule 8 compares the pattern lists alone. They are left as they are rather than replaced with a number whose meaning I would be inventing, since neither the block's count nor the anchor's explains 42; reported here and in the pull request so a reader is not misled.
